study.title: Social Media Narratives on Microplastics Claims

claims.text: Scientists have discovered that chewing gum is a massive source of microplastics, with each piece of gum potentially releasing thousands of plastic fragments into the body
claims.label: gap
claims.why: Article lists drinking water, seafood, salt, sugar, tea bags and milk as intake sources but never mentions chewing gum.
claims.author: pubity
claims.question: What claims are people making about microplastics?

claims.text: The Trump Administration added microplastics to the EPA's Contaminant Candidate List for the first time ever, shortly before July 1, 2026
claims.label: gap
claims.why: United States section covers state laws and a 2018 House amendment, not EPA listing microplastics on the Contaminant Candidate List.
claims.author: epaleezeldin
claims.verification: No source states this claim (3 nearby articles checked)
claims.question: What claims are people making about microplastics?

claims.text: Microplastics have been found in the testicles of every man studied, and in the brain, ovaries, kidneys and every organ of the human body
claims.label: gap
claims.why: Article names placenta, breast milk, brain, heart and urine in humans; testicles, ovaries and kidneys appear only in mice.
claims.author: WallStreetApes
claims.question: What claims are people making about microplastics?

claims.text: Plastic bottles contain 250,000 microplastics per liter
claims.label: contradicts
claims.why: Article reports an average of 325 particles per liter in bottled water (930 at most), far below the claimed 250,000.
claims.author: WallStreetApes
claims.verification: No source states this claim (1 nearby articles checked)
claims.question: What claims are people making about microplastics?

claims.text: Recent scientific studies have detected microplastic particles in human blood, lungs, placentas, and cardiac tissue
claims.label: gap
claims.why: Article names placenta, brain, heart and urine but never says microplastics have been found in human blood or lungs.
claims.author: GYRUS SULCUS
claims.question: What claims are people making about microplastics?

claims.text: A study in the European Heart Journal found detectable micro- and nanoplastics in the coronary blood of 84.2% of severe active heart attack (STEMI) patients, compared with 40% of patients with stable chronic heart disease and 31.8% of controls with healthy arteries
claims.label: gap
claims.why: Article cites a 2024 arterial plaque study only; no mention of the European Heart Journal coronary blood findings in heart attack patients.
claims.author: paulsaladinomd
claims.question: What claims are people making about microplastics?

claims.text: In the European Heart Journal study, polyethylene was the primary plastic found, detected in 97% of plastic-positive samples
claims.label: gap
claims.why: Article says polyethylene accumulates in the brain, but not that it made up 97% of plastic in heart attack patients.
claims.author: paulsaladinomd
claims.question: What claims are people making about microplastics?

claims.text: In the study, micro- and nanoplastic detection was highest in smokers, who had a 5.7x increased likelihood, and in individuals exposed to fine air pollution above PM2.5 of 15; researchers hypothesize smoking and airborne particulate matter compromise lung tissue barriers, and that inhalation and consumption are the primary routes of exposure
claims.label: gap
claims.why: Article does not link microplastic levels to smoking or air pollution; Oral intake calls ingestion the main exposure pathway.
claims.author: paulsaladinomd
claims.question: What claims are people making about microplastics?

claims.text: Microplastics have been found in the muscle tissue of anchovies and ribbonfish caught off the Vizag coast, meaning they are present in the edible part of the fish and not just the gut
claims.label: gap
claims.why: Article discusses microplastics in seafood generally, not in the edible muscle of fish such as anchovies and ribbonfish.
claims.author: hyderabaddoctor
claims.question: What claims are people making about microplastics?

claims.text: Wear from tires is the largest source of microplastics in nature
claims.label: gap
claims.why: Article says tire emissions exceed brakes, turf and road markings and are 5-10% of ocean plastics, but not the largest source overall.
claims.author: EenVandaag
claims.question: What claims are people making about microplastics?

claims.text: In mice, the probiotic strain found in kimchi more than doubled the excretion of nanoplastics
claims.label: gap
claims.why: Article covers gut effects of microplastics but no probiotic or kimchi strain that increases nanoplastic excretion.
claims.author: OMGFacts
claims.question: What claims are people making about microplastics?

claims.text: Research Scientist Dr. Pennate Bruce-Vanderpuije said the CSIR-Water Research Institute study found significantly higher levels of microplastics in cage-farmed tilapia than in wild fish from the Lower Volta Basin
claims.label: gap
claims.why: Article has no farmed versus wild fish comparison and no Ghanaian or Lower Volta Basin study.
claims.author: Citi973
claims.question: What claims are people making about microplastics?

claims.text: Researchers at McGill University found that a single plastic tea bag releases 11.6 billion microplastic particles into one cup (Hernandez et al., Environmental Science & Technology, 2019)
claims.label: gap
claims.why: Article lists tea bags as an intake source but gives no figure; nothing on McGill's 2019 estimate of 11.6 billion particles per cup.
claims.author: Grocery Exposed
claims.verification: No source states this claim (1 nearby articles checked)
claims.question: What claims are YouTube videos making about microplastics?

claims.text: The Autonomous University of Barcelona confirmed in 2024 (Chemosphere Journal) that polypropylene tea bags release about 1.2 billion particles per mL, which were absorbed by human intestinal cells and found in the cell nucleus
claims.label: gap
claims.why: Article lists tea bags but not the 2024 Barcelona study of polypropylene tea bags or particle uptake by intestinal cells.
claims.author: Grocery Exposed
claims.verification: No source states this claim (2 nearby articles checked)
claims.question: What claims are YouTube videos making about microplastics?

claims.text: The FDA has set no limits for microplastics in food or drink
claims.label: gap
claims.why: United States section covers state bans, a California definition and a 2018 amendment; it says nothing on FDA limits for food or drink.
claims.author: Grocery Exposed
claims.verification: No source states this claim (2 nearby articles checked)
claims.question: What claims are YouTube videos making about microplastics?

claims.text: Toxic microplastics were found in 26 toothpastes
claims.label: gap
claims.why: Article mentions toothpaste only for the US microbead phase-out; no 2026 Bangladesh study finding microplastics in 26 toothpaste brands.
claims.author: Campus Times
claims.question: What claims are YouTube videos making about microplastics?

claims.text: A recent study found indications of microplastic particles in various edible oils, including soybean oil
claims.label: gap
claims.why: Oral intake lists water, seafood, salt, sugar, tea bags and milk, but not edible oils such as soybean oil.
claims.author: Jago Live
claims.question: What claims are YouTube videos making about microplastics?

claims.text: Research on the long-term health effects of microplastics is still ongoing and definitive conclusions about health concerns have not yet been reached
claims.label: covered
claims.why: Human health already says impacts are still being tested and causation for associated conditions is unknown.
claims.author: PureAi
claims.question: What claims are YouTube videos making about microplastics?

claims.text: Some plastic containers can release microplastics into food or drinks when hot food or hot drinks are placed in them
claims.label: gap
claims.why: Section says containers shed microplastics but not that heat increases release; heat appears only under Baby bottles.
claims.author: PureAi
claims.question: What claims are YouTube videos making about microplastics?

claims.text: Research reveals that microplastics have invaded the abyssal ocean trenches, the deepest and most remote part of the ocean
claims.label: gap
claims.why: Article notes deep ocean sediment layers and high mountains but never mentions microplastics in hadal or abyssal trenches.
claims.author: Azteca Noticias
claims.question: What claims are YouTube videos making about microplastics?

claims.text: The claim that people ingest a credit card's worth of microplastics per week is based on a flawed study in which lab equipment contaminated the data
claims.label: gap
claims.why: Contested studies covers brain-tissue and glove contamination; the article never states or disputes the credit-card-per-week figure.
claims.author: Dan Go
claims.question: What claims are YouTube videos making about microplastics?

claims.text: There is no established evidence that microplastics harm human health
claims.label: contradicts
claims.why: Article cites early evidence of harm and a 2024 study linking arterial-plaque microplastics to heart attack, stroke and death.
claims.author: Dan Go
claims.question: What claims are YouTube videos making about microplastics?

claims.text: Microplastics accumulated in soil are absorbed by plant roots and accumulate inside fruits and vegetables such as apples and carrots
claims.label: covered
claims.why: Oral intake already says microplastics move from roots into stems, leaves and fruits.
claims.author: EBS 컬렉션 - 사이언스
claims.verification: No source states this claim (1 nearby articles checked)
claims.question: What claims are YouTube videos making about microplastics?

claims.text: South Korean researchers found that microplastics pass through the placenta, amniotic fluid, umbilical cord blood, and breast milk of pregnant women
claims.label: gap
claims.why: Article names placenta and breast milk but not amniotic fluid, umbilical cord blood, or the South Korean study.
claims.author: EBS 컬렉션 - 사이언스
claims.question: What claims are YouTube videos making about microplastics?

claims.text: Nanoplastics are particles so small that human kidneys cannot filter them out; they remain in the bloodstream and have been found in breast milk
claims.label: gap
claims.why: Nanoplastics section says particles cross cell membranes but nothing on kidneys failing to filter them or persistence in blood.
